title: Palladius local field-register soil probes with context-specific outcomes
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Palladius Opus agriculturae I.V introduces a field and local regions, then runs several explicitly different probes against the locally selected soil. A finite constructor keeps the introduced FIELD/REGION/SAMPLE registers and lets the same PIT_REFILL operator resolve excess returned soil as fertile, deficit as lean, and equality as moderate. The passage separately binds a clod-glue probe, a taste sample from the most-displeasing region, and vine-sign observations; no whole sentence is treated as an opaque macro.

source.work: Palladius, Opus agriculturae, Book I, chapter V, sections 1–4, De qualitate terrarum
source.source_span: The complete soil-quality subsection from the search for fertility and rejection of defective soils through vegetation signs, clod/glue test, pit refill test, taste test on the most-displeasing field part, and vineyard signs.
source.provenance: The Latin Wikisource page and Perseus CTS Latin witness were used as source navigation. Palladius is a late Roman agricultural author; no claim is made that the page is a single medieval manuscript or that its agricultural terminology maps to a target language.

duplicate_screen.checked: IDEA000425 Cato attached propagation; IDEA000321/IDEA000439 Columella/Palladius graft methods; IDEA000456 Justinian nature-dependent control; raw_common_measure_rational_accounts Fibonacci register reductions; route-check local register/reference construction.
duplicate_screen.difference: The graft cards track host/donor transformation and refusal, and the Fibonacci card tracks rational calculation registers. This card instead uses a locally introduced FIELD and REGION with one source-owned diagnostic operator whose branch result changes with the observed residual relation (excess, deficit, equality), while separate probe methods retain their own result types.

presuppositions: A field is introduced as the object being evaluated; a region can be selected within it and remains the referent of later local deictic expressions.
Fertility, sweetness, and suitability are distinct properties; one probe cannot silently stand for all of them.
The pit test compares returned earth with the excavated capacity; excess, deficit, and exact fit are source-distinct branches.
The taste test samples the part of the field that displeases most; this local reference is not replaced by the nearest previously mentioned soil.
Vegetation signs are evidence about soil/vine suitability, not proof of a target plant identity.

clauses.content: Seek fertility and reject white/bare clod, unmixed poor sand, lone chalk, barren gravel, salty or bitter soil, waterlogged soil, and similarly defective kinds.
Plants that emerge should neither be rough nor scorched nor lacking natural sap; useful signs include crops/grass/clover and fat brambles, while color is less important than fatness and sweetness.
To recognize a fat clod, sprinkle a small clod with sweet water and knead it; if it is sticky and adheres, fatness is present.
Dig and refill a pit: surplus returned earth means fat soil, deficient earth means lean soil, and an equal level means moderate soil.
Sweetness is recognized by tasting a clod moistened with sweet water in an earthen vessel, taken from the part of the field that displeases most.
Vineyard suitability uses further signs: somewhat open color/body, and shoots that are smooth, bright, tall, and fruitful, not twisted, barren, or weakened by leanness.
The same source keeps the vineyard observation distinct from the earlier general field pit and taste tests; no single result is assigned to every probe.

complete_examples.reference_resolution: P1 is the locally introduced pit in R1; SURPLUS resolves the branch without replacing R1 by a global field default.
The same PIT_REFILL operator and same field register resolve to a different result because the locally introduced region/pit observation is DEFICIT.
Equality is a third source branch, not a default or alias for either surplus or deficit.
The written local selector binds the taste sample to the most-displeasing region, not automatically to R1/R2/R3 or the nearest prior clod.

global_rules: Each FIELD is introduced before its REGION, PIT, or SAMPLE references; later deictic references resolve to the active local register explicitly selected by the source clause.
PIT_REFILL branches on exactly three mutually exclusive observations: SURPLUS -> FAT_SOIL, DEFICIT -> LEAN_SOIL, EQUAL_LEVEL -> MODERATE_SOIL.
TEST_CLOD_GLUE requires the introduced clod and sweet-water argument; sticky adhesion yields FAT_SOIL but does not yield SWEETNESS_OBSERVED unless the separate taste operator is present.
TASTE requires the source-selected PART_MOST_DISPLEASING region, a sample, water, and vessel; its output is SWEETNESS_OBSERVED, not a pit fertility class.
VINEYARD signs remain a separate result channel; no local sample or pit result is silently copied into the vineyard observation.
The rival nearest-register resolver may use an earlier sample only when the source explicitly repeats that reference; otherwise the locally introduced register is required.
constructor.observable_consequence: Changing only the locally bound PIT_REFILL observation changes the complete source result among FAT_SOIL, LEAN_SOIL, and MODERATE_SOIL. Changing the method to TASTE changes the output type to SWEETNESS_OBSERVED and requires the source's PART_MOST_DISPLEASING register; a nearest-register or one-result-for-all-probes rival cannot preserve these source distinctions.

rivals.R_FIRST_BRANCH_ONLY: Every PIT_REFILL returns FAT_SOIL, losing the source's explicit deficit and equal branches.
rivals.R_NEAREST_REGISTER: The taste phrase binds to the most recent clod or region instead of the explicitly selected most-displeasing field part.
rivals.R_ONE_SOIL_RESULT: Clod adhesion, pit residual, taste, and vineyard signs are collapsed into one generic FERTILE result, losing the source's typed result channels.

falsifier: Reject the constructor if the complete source text cannot preserve the three pit branches, the separate taste sample selector, and the vineyard sign channel under one register discipline. A target use would have no force unless local introduction, reference selector, test method, and result branch were independently visible; filling these fields occurrence by occurrence would be free fitting.
dependencies: FIELD, REGION, PIT, and SAMPLE are source-side registers introduced by the hypothetical constructor; they are not target word meanings.
The source states the branch outcomes for pit residuals but does not supply a numeric threshold or modern soil taxonomy; none is added.
The taste test records the source's sample location and observation type without inventing a sweetness threshold.
The complete source account is limited to Book I chapter V sections 1–4; no later Palladius chapter or target material is imported.
access: No Voynich target rows, images, reserves, f84/f84r/f116v, root experiment files, route, ledger, or frozen source packet were opened or changed.
